introduction: This spec defines the `Backend` Protocol and `create_backend()` factory for the `agentfox` session layer, decoupling session logic from the concrete `ClaudeBackend` implementation and enabling future alternative LLM backends without modifying `session.py`. Note: requirements referencing `agentfox` internal module paths are based on the PRD description and should be cross-checked against the installed codebase before implementation.

glossary.ActivityCallback: A callback type defined in `agentfox/ui/progress.py`: `Callable[[ActivityEvent], None]` — a synchronous callback that receives `ActivityEvent` objects for UI updates.
glossary.ActivityEvent: An event object defined in `agentfox/ui/progress.py` passed to `ActivityCallback` for UI progress updates.
glossary.AgentMessage: A type alias defined in `session/backends/types.py`: `AgentMessage = ToolUseMessage | AssistantMessage | ResultMessage`.
glossary.AssistantMessage: A message dataclass defined in `session/backends/types.py` representing a text response from the agent.
glossary.Backend: A `typing.Protocol` class (runtime-checkable) in `session/backends/protocol.py` that defines the contract any backend adapter must satisfy: `execute()`, `close()`, and `name`.
glossary.ClaudeBackend: The existing concrete backend class in `session/backends/claude.py` that wraps the Anthropic claude-agent-sdk and already satisfies the `Backend` Protocol structurally.
glossary.ConfigError: A custom exception class at `agentfox.core.errors.ConfigError` raised for configuration-related errors such as unknown backend names or missing SDK dependencies.
glossary.OrchestratorConfig: A pydantic `BaseModel` in `core/config.py` that holds orchestrator-level configuration fields including `parallel`, `session_timeout`, and now `backend`.
glossary.PermissionCallback: A callback type defined in `session/backends/types.py`: `Callable[[str, dict[str, Any]], Awaitable[bool]]` — takes a tool name and tool input and returns whether the tool call is allowed.
glossary.ResultMessage: A message dataclass defined in `session/backends/types.py` representing a final result from the agent.
glossary.SDK_CONTAINMENT: A dictionary in `test_protocol.py` mapping SDK name strings to their designated backend file, used to enforce that SDK imports are isolated to their respective backend modules.
glossary.ToolUseMessage: A message dataclass defined in `session/backends/types.py` representing a tool invocation from the agent.
glossary.agentfox: The Python package under `packages/agentfox/agentfox/` that contains the session, backend, core, and UI modules for the agent orchestration system.
glossary.archetype: An optional string parameter on `Backend.execute()` that specifies the agent archetype configuration to apply.
glossary.claude_agent_sdk: The Python SDK package required by `ClaudeBackend`, referenced as a bare module name string in containment tests.
glossary.compaction: A boolean parameter on `Backend.execute()` that controls whether context compaction is applied during session execution.
glossary.create_backend: A factory function in `session/backends/__init__.py` that accepts a backend name string and returns a `Backend` instance using lazy imports.
glossary.effort: A string parameter on `Backend.execute()` that maps to a reasoning/effort level for models that support it; valid values are `'low'`, `'medium'`, `'high'`, `'xhigh'`, and `'max'`.
glossary.lazy import: An import statement placed inside a function body rather than at module level, so the dependency is only loaded when that function is called.
glossary.node_id: An optional string parameter on `Backend.execute()` that identifies the orchestration graph node associated with a session execution.
glossary.run_session: The primary entry-point function in `session/session.py` that drives an agent session end-to-end, accepting an optional `Backend` instance.
glossary.runtime_checkable: A decorator from `typing` that allows `isinstance()` checks against a `Protocol` class at runtime, performing presence-only attribute verification.
glossary.shallow_merge: An existing function in `core/config.py` that merges global and local TOML config sections by replacing sections wholesale when the local TOML explicitly provides them.
glossary.tool_error_callback: An `Any | None` parameter on `Backend.execute()` for an as-yet-untyped callback invoked on tool errors; typed as `Any` to avoid premature coupling to `ClaudeBackend`-specific types.

user_story.goal: implement a class that satisfies a well-defined `Backend` Protocol
user_story.benefit: I can integrate a new LLM backend without modifying `session.py` or other core modules

acceptance_criteria.action: defines a `@runtime_checkable` `typing.Protocol` class named `Backend` with three members: an `execute()` async method returning `AsyncIterator[AgentMessage]`, an async `close()` method, and a `name` property returning `str`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: The class is importable as `from agentfox.session.backends import Backend` and passes `isinstance(ClaudeBackend(), Backend)` returning `True`

acceptance_criteria.action: accepts `prompt: str` as a positional argument and keyword-only arguments `system_prompt: str`, `model: str`, `cwd: str`, `permission_callback: PermissionCallback | None = None`, `activity_callback: ActivityCallback | None = None`, `tool_error_callback: Any | None = None`, `node_id: str = ''`, `archetype: str | None = None`, `max_turns: int | None = None`, `max_budget_usd: float | None = None`, `thinking: dict[str, Any] | None = None`, `effort: str | None = None`, `compaction: bool = False`, and returns `AsyncIterator[AgentMessage]`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Signature matches `ClaudeBackend.execute()` exactly so that `ClaudeBackend` satisfies the Protocol structurally without modification

acceptance_criteria.action: is declared `async def close(self) -> None` and is idempotent — calling it multiple times in any state (before, during, or after `execute()`) must not raise an error
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `None`; no exception raised on repeated calls

acceptance_criteria.action: is declared as a `@property` returning `str`, used to identify the backend for logging and telemetry (e.g. `'claude'`, `'deepagents'`, `'google-adk'`)
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: A non-empty string identifying the backend

acceptance_criteria.action: imports `AgentMessage`, `PermissionCallback` from `session/backends/types.py` and `ActivityCallback` from `agentfox.ui.progress`; it does not import from `claude.py` or any concrete backend module
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Module imports succeed without pulling in any SDK dependency

edge_cases.action: returns `False` from `isinstance(obj, Backend)` — the runtime check is presence-only and does not verify signatures
edge_cases.error_condition: an object is missing one or more of `execute`, `close`, or `name` attributes

edge_cases.action: silently ignores the `effort` value without raising an exception, consistent with the try/except `TypeError` with warning log pattern used by `ClaudeBackend`
edge_cases.return_contract: No exception raised; backend proceeds normally
edge_cases.error_condition: a backend implementation does not support the `effort` parameter

user_story.goal: obtain a `Backend` instance by name without importing concrete backend classes directly
user_story.benefit: I can switch backends via configuration without changing `session.py` and SDK dependencies are only loaded when needed

acceptance_criteria.action: uses a lazy import of `ClaudeBackend` inside the function body, instantiates it, and returns the instance typed as `Backend`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Returns a `Backend` instance where `isinstance(result, Backend)` is `True` and `result.name == 'claude'`

acceptance_criteria.action: accepts a single positional argument `name: str` (not `Literal`) to avoid coupling the signature to the set of valid backend names, which grows with each new backend spec
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Function signature is `def create_backend(name: str) -> Backend`

acceptance_criteria.action: imports backend-specific SDK modules (`claude_agent_sdk` and any future SDKs) inside the function body only, never at module level, so that importing `session/backends/__init__.py` does not load any SDK
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `claude_agent_sdk` does not appear in `sys.modules` after importing `agentfox.session.backends` unless `create_backend('claude')` has been called

acceptance_criteria.action: raises `ConfigError` with a message identifying the unknown name and listing valid backends, e.g. `"Unknown backend: 'foo'. Valid backends are: ['claude']"`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Raises `agentfox.core.errors.ConfigError`
acceptance_criteria.trigger: called with an unrecognised backend name (e.g. `'foo'`, `''`)

acceptance_criteria.action: catches the `ImportError` and raises `ConfigError` with an installation hint message, e.g. `'Backend "claude" requires claude-agent-sdk. Install it with: pip install claude-agent-sdk'`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Raises `agentfox.core.errors.ConfigError` with install hint
acceptance_criteria.trigger: the lazy import of the required SDK raises `ImportError` (SDK not installed)

acceptance_criteria.action: propagates `ConfigError` immediately to the caller with no fallback to any other backend — no silent recovery is attempted
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `ConfigError` raised; no alternative backend instantiated

edge_cases.action: raises `ConfigError` with the same unrecognised-name message path as any other unknown name

propagates the `ConfigError` through the existing exception-handling pipeline in `session.py` and the engine layer to the top-level caller; no fallback backend is selected and no process termination occurs — the error is signaled via exception only
edge_cases.return_contract: `ConfigError` propagated to top-level caller; no process exit
edge_cases.error_condition: `create_backend()` raises `ConfigError` during session startup due to missing SDK or invalid name

user_story.goal: specify the desired backend in the TOML config file
user_story.benefit: I can switch backends without modifying source code, and invalid backend names are caught at config-load time with a clear error

acceptance_criteria.action: adds a field `backend: Literal["claude"] = "claude"` to the pydantic `BaseModel`, making `'claude'` the default value so that existing config files omitting the field continue to work
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `OrchestratorConfig().backend == 'claude'`

acceptance_criteria.action: is config-file only — no environment variable override is provided, consistent with all other `OrchestratorConfig` fields
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Field is not settable via environment variable

acceptance_criteria.action: pydantic raises `ValidationError` which the existing `load_config()` catches and re-raises as `ConfigError` with a user-friendly message — no additional error-handling code is required for the `backend` field
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Raises `agentfox.core.errors.ConfigError`
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a TOML config file contains an invalid `backend` value (not in `Literal["claude"]`)

acceptance_criteria.action: inherits the global TOML `[orchestrator]` section wholesale, including the `backend` field value
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Merged config `backend` equals the global TOML value
acceptance_criteria.state: local TOML omits the `[orchestrator]` section entirely

acceptance_criteria.action: applies the pydantic default `'claude'` for the `backend` field; the global TOML's `backend` value is not inherited for this field
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Merged config `backend == 'claude'`

edge_cases.action: pydantic validation fails and `load_config()` re-raises as `ConfigError` without reaching `create_backend()`
edge_cases.return_contract: Raises `agentfox.core.errors.ConfigError` with pydantic-generated field validation message
edge_cases.error_condition: TOML file provides `backend = "unknown-value"` not present in the `Literal` type

user_story.benefit: mypy resolves `AsyncIterator[AgentMessage]` correctly through the Protocol, eliminating the `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` suppression comment

acceptance_criteria.action: changes the `backend` parameter type from `ClaudeBackend | None` to `Backend | None`, and when `backend` is `None` instantiates the backend by calling `create_backend(config.orchestrator.backend)` using the config-validated name
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `run_session()` behaves identically to the previous implementation when called with `backend=None` and default config

acceptance_criteria.action: removes the `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` comment from the `async for` loop over `backend.execute()` (previously line 256); mypy resolves the `AsyncIterator[AgentMessage]` return type through the `Backend` Protocol without suppression
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: mypy passes with no `type: ignore` suppression on that line

acceptance_criteria.action: imports `Backend` and `create_backend` from `agentfox.session.backends`; the direct import of `ClaudeBackend` is removed from `session.py`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `ClaudeBackend` does not appear in `session.py` imports

acceptance_criteria.action: all existing call sites that pass a `ClaudeBackend` instance explicitly continue to work because `ClaudeBackend` satisfies the `Backend` Protocol structurally — no call sites require updates
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: All existing session unit tests pass unmodified

edge_cases.action: `close()` is called on the `Backend` instance in a `finally` block to release any remaining resources; `close()` is idempotent so calling it after normal exhaustion is also safe
edge_cases.return_contract: `close()` called exactly once in `finally` block; no resource leak; no exception from idempotent `close()`
edge_cases.error_condition: session execution is cancelled mid-stream via asyncio task cancellation or `asyncio.wait_for()` timeout

edge_cases.action: the error propagates to the caller via exception; `run_session()` does not call `close()` (no backend was created) and does not terminate the process
edge_cases.return_contract: `ConfigError` propagated; no process exit; no orphaned backend instance

user_story.benefit: I have a stable, documented import path for the backend abstraction

acceptance_criteria.action: updates `__all__` to include `'Backend'` and `'create_backend'` in addition to the existing exports (`'AgentMessage'`, `'AssistantMessage'`, `'ClaudeBackend'`, `'PermissionCallback'`, `'ResultMessage'`, `'ToolUseMessage'`)
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `from agentfox.session.backends import Backend, create_backend` succeeds without error

acceptance_criteria.action: does NOT add `Backend` or `create_backend` to `session/__init__.py` or `agentfox/__init__.py` — consumers must import directly from `agentfox.session.backends`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `from agentfox import Backend` raises `ImportError`; `from agentfox.session import Backend` raises `ImportError`

user_story.goal: enforce that `ClaudeBackend` satisfies `Backend` at runtime and that SDK imports are isolated to their designated files
user_story.benefit: regressions in Protocol compliance or accidental SDK coupling are caught on every PR

acceptance_criteria.action: creates a new test file that asserts `isinstance(ClaudeBackend(), Backend)` returns `True`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: pytest passes; assertion holds

acceptance_criteria.action: scans all `.py` files under `packages/agentfox/agentfox/` recursively using `glob.glob(os.path.join(agent_fox_dir, '**', '*.py'), recursive=True)`, asserts each SDK name string in `SDK_CONTAINMENT` appears **only** in its designated file using substring match, and excludes the designated file itself from that assertion
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: pytest passes; any non-designated file containing an SDK name string causes the test to fail with a clear message identifying the offending file and SDK name

acceptance_criteria.action: is defined as a dictionary `{'claude_agent_sdk': 'claude.py'}` with placeholder comments for future backends (`deepagents`, `google-adk`); adding a new backend requires only a one-line addition to the mapping
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Dictionary is extensible; test logic does not change when entries are added

acceptance_criteria.action: targets only `packages/agentfox/agentfox/` (production source); `packages/agentfox/tests/` is a sibling directory outside the glob path and is never scanned, so SDK name strings in mock/patch strings within test files do not trigger false positives
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: No false positives from test file content; glob never reaches `tests/` directory

acceptance_criteria.system: CI enforcement of protocol and containment tests
acceptance_criteria.action: both the `isinstance` test and the containment property test run as required checks on every PR via the existing CI pipeline
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: PR cannot merge if either test fails

edge_cases.action: test fails with a descriptive assertion message identifying the SDK name and the offending file path
edge_cases.return_contract: pytest reports failure; CI blocks the PR
edge_cases.error_condition: an SDK name string from `SDK_CONTAINMENT` appears in a non-designated production source file (accidental coupling)

edge_cases.action: test raises a clear error (e.g. via `assert os.path.isdir(agent_fox_dir)`) rather than silently passing with zero files scanned
edge_cases.return_contract: pytest reports failure with descriptive message; empty scan does not produce a false pass
edge_cases.error_condition: `packages/agentfox/agentfox/` directory does not exist or cannot be read at test time

correctness_properties.title: Lazy import isolation: `claude_agent_sdk` not loaded unless backend is selected
correctness_properties.for_any: Python process that imports `agentfox.session.backends` without calling `create_backend('claude')`

correctness_properties.title: `create_backend()` always returns a `Backend` instance or raises `ConfigError`
correctness_properties.invariant: the function either returns an object where `isinstance(result, Backend)` is `True`, or raises `agentfox.core.errors.ConfigError` — no other outcome is possible

correctness_properties.title: `close()` is idempotent across all states
correctness_properties.for_any: `Backend` instance `b` in any state (before, during, or after `execute()`)
correctness_properties.invariant: calling `b.close()` any number of times does not raise an exception

correctness_properties.title: SDK containment: each SDK string appears only in its designated file
correctness_properties.for_any: every `.py` file under `packages/agentfox/agentfox/` except the designated backend file
correctness_properties.invariant: the SDK name string (e.g. `'claude_agent_sdk'`) does not appear as a substring in the file's contents

correctness_properties.title: Existing session tests pass unmodified after type widening
correctness_properties.for_any: test in the existing session unit test suite
correctness_properties.invariant: the test passes without modification after `run_session()` parameter type is widened from `ClaudeBackend | None` to `Backend | None`

correctness_properties.title: mypy passes with no `type: ignore` suppression on `async for backend.execute()`
correctness_properties.for_any: static analysis run of `session/session.py` with mypy
correctness_properties.invariant: no `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` comment is present on the `async for` loop over `backend.execute()`, and mypy reports no errors on that statement

execution_paths.title: Session startup with default claude backend via config

steps.action: starts a session without specifying a `backend` argument; TOML config has `backend = 'claude'` (or omits it, getting the default)
detects `backend` parameter is `None` and calls `create_backend(config.orchestrator.backend)` with `'claude'`
lazily imports `ClaudeBackend` from `session/backends/claude.py`, instantiates it, and returns the instance as `Backend`
calls `backend.execute(prompt, ...)` and iterates over the resulting `AsyncIterator[AgentMessage]` without a `# type: ignore` comment
yields `AgentMessage` instances (tool use, assistant text, or result) to the session loop
calls `backend.close()` in the `finally` block after the iterator is exhausted or on cancellation

execution_paths.title: Session startup fails with unknown backend name

steps.action: pydantic `Literal` validation fails; `load_config()` catches `ValidationError` and re-raises as `ConfigError` identifying the invalid `backend` value
receives `ConfigError` and surfaces it to the user as a configuration error message; no session is started

execution_paths.title: Session startup fails with missing SDK

steps.action: calls `run_session()` with default config (`backend='claude'`) on a system where `claude_agent_sdk` is not installed
attempts lazy import of `ClaudeBackend`; `ImportError` is raised by the Python import system
catches `ImportError` and raises `ConfigError` with install hint: `'Backend "claude" requires claude-agent-sdk. Install it with: pip install claude-agent-sdk'`
receives `ConfigError` and surfaces the install hint to the user; no session is started and no process is terminated

execution_paths.title: Containment test enforces SDK isolation on PR

steps.action: opens a PR that accidentally imports `claude_agent_sdk` in a non-backend production file
scans all `.py` files under `packages/agentfox/agentfox/` using glob, finds `claude_agent_sdk` in a non-designated file, and fails the assertion
marks the PR check as failed and blocks merge; the developer receives a descriptive error message identifying the offending file

error_handling.behavior: Raises `agentfox.core.errors.ConfigError` with message identifying the unknown name and listing valid backends, e.g. `"Unknown backend: 'foo'. Valid backends are: ['claude']"`; no fallback is attempted

error_handling.condition: Required SDK not installed when `create_backend()` attempts lazy import
error_handling.behavior: Catches `ImportError` and raises `agentfox.core.errors.ConfigError` with a `pip install` hint specific to the missing SDK; no fallback backend is selected

error_handling.condition: Invalid `backend` literal value read from TOML config file
error_handling.behavior: pydantic raises `ValidationError`; `load_config()` catches it and re-raises as `agentfox.core.errors.ConfigError` with a user-friendly message; `create_backend()` is never reached

error_handling.condition: `ConfigError` raised during session startup (missing SDK or invalid name)
error_handling.behavior: Propagated immediately through the existing exception-handling pipeline in `session.py` and the engine layer to the top-level caller; no fallback, no process termination — error signaled via exception only

error_handling.condition: Session cancelled mid-stream via asyncio task cancellation or `asyncio.wait_for()` timeout
error_handling.behavior: `close()` is called on the `Backend` instance in the `finally` block of `run_session()`; `close()` is idempotent so this is safe even if the iterator was already exhausted

error_handling.condition: Containment test scans a production directory that does not exist or is unreadable
error_handling.behavior: Test asserts the directory exists before scanning; fails with a descriptive error rather than silently passing with zero files scanned

error_handling.condition: SDK name string found in a non-designated production source file during containment scan
error_handling.behavior: Containment property test fails with a descriptive assertion message identifying the SDK name and offending file path; CI blocks the PR

symbols.name: Protocol
symbols.notes: Base class for structural subtyping (static duck typing). Combined with @runtime_checkable for isinstance() support.

symbols.name: runtime_checkable
symbols.notes: Decorator that enables isinstance() checks against a Protocol. Performs presence-only attribute verification, not signature verification.

symbols.name: AsyncIterator
symbols.notes: Used as the return type of Backend.execute(). AsyncGenerator is a subtype, so ClaudeBackend's async generator satisfies this.

symbols.name: Literal
symbols.notes: Used for OrchestratorConfig.backend field type: Literal["claude"]. Widened to include additional backends in future specs.

symbols.name: Any
symbols.notes: Used for tool_error_callback parameter type as Any | None — intentionally broad until a concrete cross-backend type is defined.

symbols.name: BaseModel
symbols.notes: Base class for OrchestratorConfig. Provides Literal field validation; ValidationError is caught by load_config() and re-raised as ConfigError.

symbols.name: glob
symbols.signature: glob.glob(pathname: str, *, recursive: bool = False) -> list[str]
symbols.notes: Used in test_protocol.py containment test to scan all .py files under packages/agentfox/agentfox/ recursively.
